questions.question: What is printed on the 37 structure sheets?
questions.answer: All 37 have now been read in full, 2026-11-17, and every one of the 94 schedule rows carries its fee, prize-pool split, starting stack, level time and late-registration close. The sheets are consistent on one point worth stating: $fee + $prize pool always equals the printed buy-in, on all 94 rows, with no exceptions. What they do not contain is any entry limit (FD-03) or any payout percentage on 46 rows (FD-21).
questions.how_to_close: Read each PDF linked from the official schedule page.
questions.can_be_closed_here: Closed here: every sheet is a public PDF.

questions.question: Does any Venetian one-day event actually forbid re-entry?
questions.answer: No. With all 37 sheets read, none prints a freezeout, no-rebuy or no-add-on rule. The only entry restriction in the series is the multi-flight rule, which stops a player who has already bagged chips from buying a later flight - not the same thing, and it does not apply to one-day events at all in the way it applies to flights. Four sheets had previously been recorded as forbidding a second entry on that basis; they have been corrected to sheet-silent.
questions.can_be_closed_here: Closed here: every sheet is a public PDF.
questions.blocks: The single-entry claim the brief asks for. It cannot be satisfied.
questions.resolution: Closed 2026-11-17 with a negative answer. The practical consequence is that the site cannot claim any event is single-entry, which is why the tournament page separates rows by evidence strength instead.

questions.question: Is the resort fee taxed at 13.38%, and is parking taxed?
questions.why: The properties say 'plus applicable tax' without printing the arithmetic. The calculator applies the room tax to the resort fee; that is a computation, not a quotation.
questions.how_to_close: Read the tax lines on a real checkout confirmation for one night.

questions.question: Which guarantee figures include bounties?
questions.answer: 32 of the 94 rows. The sheets print the basis explicitly: sheets 1, 8, 11, 15, 16, 26, 27, 30 and 33 define the guarantee as prize pool plus total bounties, and the wording on each names the actual composition - for example sheet 15's 'the actual prize pool plus the total amount of $100 bounties that are awarded'. The other 51 dollar guarantees are pure prize pool, and 7 rows guarantee seats instead of money.
questions.how_to_close: Read the guarantee rules on all 37 sheets and classify each.
questions.can_be_closed_here: Closed here: every sheet is a public PDF.
questions.resolution: Closed 2026-11-17. The 32 bounty-inclusive rows carry their guarantee but no guarantee-to-fee ratio, and the table prints 'n/a - bounty GTD' in that cell.

questions.question: Can the trip actually be filled from 8 AM to night?
questions.why: No event starts before 9:10 AM and the earliest one-day event is 10:10 AM, so part of the morning is free by construction.
questions.how_to_close: Accept a 10:10 AM start, or add a second venue with an earlier daily event and verify its schedule.
questions.can_be_closed_here: partly - the Venetian answer is no

questions.why: It decides how long the trip can stay flexible and whether a prepaid rate is safe.

questions.question: How many players enter each event?
questions.why: Guarantee-per-entry is a descriptive ratio. Whether a guarantee is likely to be met, and therefore whether the ratio means anything, depends on field size, which no organiser publishes in advance.
questions.how_to_close: Use historical results for the same event in earlier series if the venue publishes them.
